newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Tiatia crucial for Wgtn against Waikato.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, RUGBY UNION - Tiatia crucial for Wgtn against Waikato.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Sept 27 - Filo Tiatia lends the cutting edge to the Wellington rugby team's forwards so necessary if the side is to have any chance of beating Waikato in Sunday's big match -- and of qualifying in the first division's top four, NZPA reports.
Without his aggressive tackling and running, Wellington lack a vital power source, and ability to slip into overdrive and give back what is being received.
The agenda for Wellington over the rest of this season is quite clear.

They aim to start with a victory against Ranfurly Shield holders Waikato on Sunday. That would bring Wellington to 20 or 21 points, probably just a couple away from qualifying for the National Provincial Championship (NPC) semifinals.

The remaining two matches, away against Counties and Otago, represent two difficult assignments. Wellington were beaten 29-3 by Counties in Pukekohe two years ago, and their record at Carisbrook is little better. Both those teams are in desperate need of points themselves. To have to win both these matches to qualify is a very big task.
So when Tiatia this week talked about the need for the Wellington forwards to become mentally tougher in a hurry, he was only talking reality if the side is to qualify.
"We're slowly getting there as a team," Tiatia said. "I'm not too worried about the backs. They're doing great. If we give them the ball on a plate they put it over the line.
"So the onus goes on to all eight of us forwards, as well as those in the reserves, to get mentally tougher and do the hard work."
Waikato, in the opinion of many, will not have the collective mind on the job on Sunday because of the upcoming clash of the giants against Auckland five days later.

That would be a very foolish thought if Wellington coach Frank Walker and his players allow it. The Waikato outfit are a professional one fully aware of the need for championship points against Wellington.
Waikato have 18 points at present. If they miss out altogether against Wellington and loses the shield to Auckland, they could end up not qualifying at all for the semis.

So Tiatia and his fellow players have to shut any thought of Waikato "not being on the job" out of their minds. They have to do it all themselves. And that means further forward improvement and a tougher attitude in the set pieces, where Wellington are struggling to win their own ball.
"If we can't win our ball from set pieces, we're never going to win a game. So we're definitely going to target Waikato as a must-win," Taitia said.

Now that the big loose forward is really back into his game after a succession of injuries last year and this, he can think about his future, about whether he's better at No 7 or No 8, and whether he thinks about chasing an international jersey for the All Blacks or Samoa.
Hurricanes coach Frank Oliver went against the general feeling on Tiatia by playing him at No 7 for much of the Super 12, and now Wellington's Frank Walker has gone the same way.
"I'm enjoying No 7 but I still need more games there to learn the mechanics and get my base fitness up a bit. But I do really enjoy No 8 -- I'd be lying if I said I didn't," Tiatia said.
"However, some coaches have said I might go a little bit further as an openside flanker, so I have to weigh up both positions pretty quickly."
Tiatia, of course, has always yearned for an All Black jersey, even though his father Iete Tiatia is a backbone of local Samoan rugby. But he's having trouble convincing "the right people".
Earlier this year Samoan coach Bryan Williams suggested he change allegiances, but Tiatia says no -- at this stage anyway.

"I guess everyone's hopeful of an All Black jersey -- it's everyone's dream. Bryan is pretty keen about me coming across to help Samoa, but I've told him I'll give it another year. If the All Black jersey doesn't happen, then I guess it wasn't meant to be," Tiatia said.
"I've just got to give it everything in the remaining games of the season, and I'll go for it next year."
